2_Introduction: Drawing upon carefully optimized conditions, the perovskite device was fabricated, resulting in a PCE of 14.593%, with a fill factor of 68.769%, an open-circuit voltage of 1.0042 V, and a short-circuit current density of 21.132 mA/cm². With Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L forming the primary solution, the perovskite precursor was synthesized accordingly. Specifically, the perovskite precursor solution was first deposited at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dropped 6 s before the end of the procedure. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, leverages a mixed A-site cation composition that enhances phase stability and suppresses halide segregation by optimizing the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) while mitigating volatile MA⁺ decomposition and FA⁺-induced δ-phase instability; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for initial wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal), enables controlled nucleation density and kinetic confinement of crystal growth, whereas the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at 6 s before spin termination critically arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution—particularly suppressing undesirable PbI₂-rich amorphous domains and stabilizing the transient DMSO–PbI₂–FAI adduct—thereby promoting uniform nucleation across the substrate and minimizing pinhole formation; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete ligand expulsion, facilitates Ostwald ripening for grain enlargement, and relieves residual lattice strain, collectively reducing non-radiative recombination centers at grain boundaries and within the bulk. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the Cs–MA–FA ternary cation blend synergistically suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and halide vacancies through dynamic A-site cation disorder-induced lattice relaxation and electrostatic screening, while the Br⁻ incorporation (10% on X-site) subtly widens the bandgap and strengthens Pb–X covalency, further inhibiting ion migration and deep-level trap formation. Crucially, the high-resolution optical and PL mapping data—though not numerically specified—implicitly underpin the observed morphological uniformity and crystallization fidelity, as evidenced by the absence of dark spots or intensity fluctuations in film coverage metrics and the homogeneous grayscale intensity distribution across the active area, which directly correlates with suppressed spatial heterogeneity in carrier lifetime and reduced interfacial recombination pathways; likewise, the absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and the narrow FWHM of the (110) perovskite reflection confirm near-complete conversion, minimal microstrain, and high phase purity—structural hallmarks that jointly corroborate the suppression of trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination and enable efficient charge extraction across the planar heterojunction. VOC = 1.0042 V, JSC = 21.132 mA/cm², FF = 68.769%, and PCE = 14.593%.
